F1_display_type_split_on_SemanticAsserti.consequence_before_the_fix: PRODUCT_TYPE_BY_DISPLAY_TYPE was keyed on the label spelling only, so product_type() fell through to _snake_upper, which inserts a separator before a capital. _snake_upper('SEMANTIC_ASSERTION') is 'SEMANTIC__ASSERTION' -- a double underscore. The API therefore served one product object type under two names, one of them malformed, across 30,266 assertions; PADA_PARALLEL_GROUP (1,434 nodes) had the same defect. 31,700 of 71,373 public nodes were affected.
F1_display_type_split_on_SemanticAsserti.fix_applied: src/vedagraph/api/services/graph_service.py -- declared both spellings of each display_type in PRODUCT_TYPE_BY_DISPLAY_TYPE. Behaviour-restoring: the map's own docstring and tests/api/test_graph.py::TestLiveInvariants::test_the_product_type_map_covers_every_display_type already asserted this invariant, nothing in the repository or the frontend referenced the malformed name (grep: 0 occurrences), and frontend/src/components/lab/plates/transmission.tsx already keys on SEMANTIC_ASSERTION.
F1_display_type_split_on_SemanticAsserti.residual_NOT_fixed: The split lives in the graph, not only in the map. frontend/.world/world.raw.json carries the node `type` straight from display_type, so the shipped world bundle holds 'SEMANTIC_ASSERTION' for 30,266 nodes and 'SemanticAssertion' for 4,865 -- the only pair among its 48 node types that differs merely in spelling. Any consumer that colours, filters or legends by type sees two classes where there is one. Repairing that needs either a graph write (forbidden: the census is frozen) or an exporter normalisation plus a re-export (which would change the verified export hash). Handed to the lead as a decision, not worked around.
